title: Lecture 2 - Asymptotic Proof MCQs
description: Midterm MCQs on concepts, mathematical reasoning and proof steps. No code tracing or code-analysis questions.
subject: Algorithm Analysis

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] To bound 3n²+17n log₂ n+1000 above by a multiple of n², which inequality is useful for n≥2?
questions.explanation: Multiplying log₂ n≤n by 17n bounds the middle term by 17n².

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Which pair certifies 3n²+17n log₂ n+1000 ∈ O(n²)?
questions.explanation: For n≥2, the three terms are bounded by 3n², 17n² and 1000n², respectively.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Why does 3n²+17n log₂ n+1000 ≥ 3n² hold for n≥1?
options: Dropping positive terms increases the expression.
All lower-order terms are exactly zero.
questions.explanation: Removing nonnegative terms gives a lower bound.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] If a lower bound holds from n=1 and an upper bound from n=2, which common threshold is safe for Θ?
questions.explanation: Use the larger of the two thresholds so both inequalities hold.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Which chain proves 3n²+17n log₂ n+1000 ∈ Θ(n²)?
questions.explanation: Matching lower and upper quadratic bounds with fixed constants establish Theta.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] For f(n)=7n³+25n+60 and n≥1, which upper estimate is valid?
questions.explanation: Use n≤n³ and 1≤n³, then add coefficients: 7+25+60=92.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Which witnesses prove 7n³+25n+60 ∈ Θ(n³)?
questions.explanation: The valid bounds are 7n³≤f(n)≤92n³ for n≥1; constants must be positive and fixed.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Why can 20n be bounded above by 20n log₂ n when n≥2?
questions.explanation: Multiplying log₂ n≥1 by positive 20n gives the needed inequality.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Which upper bound follows for 50n log₂ n+20n when n≥2?
questions.explanation: The linear term is at most 20n log₂ n, so the coefficients add to 70.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Which safe constants prove 5log₂ n+100 ∈ Θ(log₂ n)?
questions.explanation: For n≥2, log₂ n≥1, so 5log₂ n≤f(n)≤105log₂ n.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] For n≥1, n³+20n²+100 is at most which simple cubic bound?
questions.explanation: Bound n² and 1 by n³, then add 1+20+100.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Why is 3n+2 not in Ω(n²)?
options: Its ratio to n² tends to infinity.
(3n+2)/n² tends to 0, so no fixed positive lower multiplier works.
It fails at n=1, which alone disproves every eventual bound.
Every linear function has a quadratic lower bound.
questions.correctAnswer: (3n+2)/n² tends to 0, so no fixed positive lower multiplier works.
questions.explanation: The ratio 3/n+2/n² approaches zero, contradicting any positive eventual lower bound.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Which chain proves 3n+2 ∈ Θ(n)?
questions.explanation: Since 2≤2n for n≥1, the upper bound is 5n; the lower bound is 3n.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Must the chosen Big-O constant c be the smallest possible?
options: Yes; otherwise the proof is invalid.
No; c may be a different number for each n.
No; any fixed positive c with a valid threshold is sufficient.
questions.correctAnswer: No; any fixed positive c with a valid threshold is sufficient.
questions.explanation: The definition requires existence of suitable constants, not optimization of them.

questions.question: For f(n)=2n², which pair of claims is true?
questions.explanation: Cubic is a looser upper bound; linear is a looser lower bound.

questions.question: Which reasoning proves n²+n ∈ O(n²)?
options: An upper bound must discard n².
questions.explanation: The lower-order n term is at most n² for n≥1.

questions.question: Is 2ⁿ ∈ Ω(10n²) for sufficiently large n?
options: No; Omega only applies to best-case algorithms.
No; any coefficient 10 makes a polynomial grow faster than an exponential.
Yes; exponential growth eventually exceeds every constant multiple needed for this quadratic lower bound.
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; exponential growth eventually exceeds every constant multiple needed for this quadratic lower bound.
questions.explanation: Exponential growth dominates polynomial growth eventually; small initial values do not decide the claim.

questions.question: Which argument shows 2ⁿ ∈ O(3ⁿ)?
options: The bases 2 and 3 are asymptotically equal constants, so both exponentials are Θ-equal.
questions.explanation: The ratio is bounded above, proving Big-O; it tends to zero, so this is not Theta.

questions.question: Why is the constant function 10 in Θ(log₂ 10)?
options: Both are positive constants independent of n.
questions.correctAnswer: Both are positive constants independent of n.
questions.explanation: A fixed logarithm of a fixed positive argument greater than 1 is itself a positive constant.

questions.question: Why is n not in O(10)?
options: For any fixed c, n eventually exceeds 10c.
Big-O cannot compare two positive functions.
questions.correctAnswer: For any fixed c, n eventually exceeds 10c.
questions.explanation: No fixed constant upper bound can contain the unbounded linear function.

questions.question: Which identity helps compare n with log₂(n²)?
questions.explanation: The power rule moves the exponent into a multiplicative constant.

questions.question: Is (log₂ n)² ∈ Θ(log₂ n+5)?
options: Yes; every expression involving log is Θ(log n).
Yes; squaring any function only changes a constant.
No; the numerator tends to zero.
No; the ratio grows without bound.
questions.correctAnswer: No; the ratio grows without bound.
questions.explanation: The denominator is Θ(log n), while the numerator has an additional unbounded log factor.

questions.question: What is insertion sort's tight best-case time on already sorted input?
questions.explanation: The outer progression still visits the elements, but little shifting is needed.

questions.question: What is insertion sort's tight worst-case time on reverse-sorted distinct input?
questions.explanation: The total shifts grow like 1+2+...+(n-1), which is quadratic.

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates notation from input cases?
options: O cannot describe a best-case function.
Ω always means best case, regardless of which function is given.
O, Ω and Θ can bound best-, worst- or average-case cost functions.
questions.correctAnswer: O, Ω and Θ can bound best-, worst- or average-case cost functions.
questions.explanation: The formal inequalities define bounds; input cases define the cost function being bounded.
